attributes.description: The high-souled hero, son of Dasaratha and Raghu's line, committed to protecting Bráhmans and fulfilling his promises.
The daughter of the Maithil monarch (Janak), wife of Ráma, described as a paragon of faithful love.
The younger brother of Ráma, devoted and faithful, who accompanies him in the forest.
A mighty hermit and saintly lord who subdued demons and humbled the Vindhya hills.
A virtuous sage whose hermitage Ráma visits and who directs Ráma to Agastya.
A hermit who follows Ráma and explains the mystery of the Panchápsaras lake.
A great votary who created the Panchápsaras lake through his rites and was seduced by five nymphs.
A holy hermit living south of SutíkshGa’s retreat, whose home Ráma visits first.
A demon who took the form of a ram to kill Bráhmans, eventually devoured and destroyed by Agastya.
A fierce demon who spoke Sanskrit to trick Bráhmans; he was consumed to dust by Agastya's glance.
The deity for whom the Heavenly Artist planned a mighty bow used to slay demon foes.
The Lord divine (Indra) who provided Ráma with a sunbright shaft and an endless quiver.
The 'Lake of the Five Nymphs,' created by MáG akarGi, featuring a hidden palace beneath the waters.
The 'best of hills' that bowed its crest at Agastya's command to allow the sun's journey.
The saintly crowd and hermits of the wood who sought Ráma's protection from fiends.
Fiends or giants of the wood who torment hermits and devour bleeding flesh.
The sacred epic detailing the journey and deeds of Ráma.

attributes.context: Husband and wife; Ráma vows to protect her and values her affection.
Brothers; LakshmaG is Ráma's devoted companion and guardian.
Ráma swears an oath to protect the Bráhmans from the giants of the wood.
Agastya devoured Vátápi to end his slaughter of Bráhmans.
Agastya destroyed Ilval with a single glance of fury.
Agastya commanded the mountain to bow its crest.
SutíkshGa provides the directions and path for Ráma to find Agastya.
The sage created and performed penance within the lake.
Ráma visits Agastya to seek his favor and receive divine weapons.
Both are deities whose weapons (bow and shaft) are passed to Ráma by Agastya.
